nv_main_wall.blurb: A west-facing crag in the river canyon between Reno and Truckee, also called Lower River Rock. Most of its sixteen lines are trad, mainly cracks and flakes, with a few bolted lines and a couple of top ropes. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.11, with the largest cluster around 5.10. Since the wall faces west it warms up after midday, which makes it a popular choice when the weather is cold. Many of the easier climbs are simple to rig for top rope, so it works well for climbers learning to place gear and lead.
nv_main_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the dirt pullout beside the interstate on the river side, reached by leaving at the Farad exit.
nv_main_wall.approach: Go through the gate, follow the dirt road a short way, then take the trail down to the railroad tracks. Cross the tracks, walk over the footbridge above the river and a second small walkway; the wall sits on your right.

nv_the_monument.blurb: A string of single-pitch sandstone cliffs just outside the mouth of Black Velvet Canyon in Red Rock, on the right as you look up the canyon. Nearly all of the sixteen lines are trad, with a single bolted route among them. Difficulty starts around 5.9, builds through a solid block of 5.10s, 5.11s and 5.12s, and tops out with one 5.13. A large triangular roof split by a clean crack is the most recognisable feature. Many descents are by rappel, which can call for two ropes.

nv_tsunami_boulder.blurb: The first big boulder you meet on the trail into the Washoe Boulders, in the hills above Carson City. Its main face is steep and overhanging, with sixteen problems packed tightly enough that variations and links come easily. Grades spread from V0 to V7: most sit between V0 and V3, with a small group of harder problems from V5 up. The rock is rough and hard on the fingertips. The boulder faces north, so it stays shaded through summer, though the area as a whole can run hot.

nv_rattlsnake_crag_climbs.blurb: A long, low, south-facing cliff about 35 feet tall in the Henderson Crags, on the edge of Henderson near the McCullough Hills. Sixteen climbs are logged here, mostly short trad lines with a few bolted routes, a couple of top ropes and one boulder problem. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.11, with most around 5.9 and 5.10. It makes an easy afternoon outing. The top edge is rotten, so build any anchor well back from the lip. Small boulders sit in the wash below.
nv_rattlsnake_crag_climbs.parking_note: Use the McCullough Hills trailhead at the west end of E Mission Dr in Henderson; the cliff can be seen from the lot.
nv_rattlsnake_crag_climbs.approach: Follow the concrete-lined drainage channel north for a short walk; the cliff is in view from the start.

nv_hunter_s_thompson_dome.blurb: A dome-shaped sandstone wall in the Calico Hills at Red Rock, reached from the Second Pullout. Sixteen routes mix a larger group of bolted sport lines with some older trad lines, spanning 5.8 to the 5.11s, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. A wide roof breaks the right side of the face. The wall is taller than its neighbours and feels more like an adventure than a roadside crag. A 60 m rope handles most lines, and a 70 m can help on the longest. It faces west to southwest, so mornings are shaded. Climbers who top out can walk off.

nv_glass_house_the.blurb: A compact, steep limestone sport cliff along Route 158 in the Spring Mountains outside Las Vegas, sitting just south of Robbers Roost at roughly 8,000 feet. All sixteen climbs are bolted. The grades are demanding: a few 5.11s, then mostly 5.12 and 5.13, with one harder line above that. The wall faces east and sees sun only in the morning, which makes it a sensible refuge from valley summer heat. It rewards strong sport climbers rather than beginners.
